A drawing of the typical spot, not a photo of this car. Locations come from descriptions (klavkarr.com, owner forums) and may differ by year and trim.

string-array.name: guide_steps
string-array.item: How to test
1. Ignition on, engine off. \"Connect\" → adapter.
2. Wait until \"Scanning the car…\" disappears on \"Main\". The first time takes a few minutes.
3. Start the engine, idle for 5–10 minutes.
4. Drive 20–40 minutes: city, steady 60 and 90 km/h, accelerations, one full-throttle run.
5. At idle: \"Codes\" → \"Read\", \"Info\" → \"Mode 06\".
6. Stop the engine, tap ✕ at the top, ⇪ to send the session.
Don\'t touch the phone while driving. Don\'t clear codes.

string-array.name: guide_more_steps
string-array.item: Step by step

Connecting: the app reads everything it can on its own: PIDs, VIN, trouble codes, freeze frame, readiness monitors, on-board tests (Mode 06), modules and their codes. \"Info\" shows the protocol (CAN — ISO 15765-4, K-line — ISO 9141-2 or ISO 14230), VIN and make.
The first connection to a car takes longer: the app searches for modules. After that they are remembered by VIN, and connecting takes under a minute.
A cold start is more useful than a warm one: you can see coolant and oil temperatures rise and idle RPM come down.

The open tab decides what is read more often. \"Fuel\": fuel trims, O2 and per-cylinder misfires. \"Main\": the essentials. \"All data\" polls everything in turn, so each parameter updates less often; it\'s worse for a drive.
Noticed something odd (a jerk, a stumble, a misfire)? Note the time: everything in the logs is timestamped.

After a drive, pending codes and on-board test results that weren\'t there when parked may appear. \"Rescan\" on \"Info\" refreshes the readiness monitors, \"Read all modules\" on \"Codes\" reads the code memory of all modules.
You can turn the screen off: recording continues in the background, with a notification in the notification shade.

string-array.name: guide_gm
string-array.item: GM

First connection: module search on HS-CAN (~1 min), module identification and full code memory ($A9). While reading codes, the adapter switches to raw frame mode and then back; if it doesn\'t respond, it re-initializes itself.

About 45 GM parameters ($22) are polled: engine and transmission oil, torque converter slip, transmission shaft speeds, knock, per-cylinder misfires. Parameters marked \"(?)\" are verified against only one source.
Airbags, instrument cluster, radio, climate and TPMS are on single-wire GMLAN (pin 1); a regular ELM327 can\'t see them.
If the engine firmware is modified (open loop, O2 sensors or catalysts disabled), fuel trims stay at 0 and the O2 sensors don\'t change — this is not an app fault.

string-array.name: guide_vag
string-array.item: Volkswagen
A Polo 9N (up to about 2009) with a petrol engine is usually on K-line. Then only standard OBD is read — no module search, part numbers or module codes (see Toyota).
First connection: VW module search (~2 min, addresses 7E0–7E7 and 700–775), module identification (part number, software version, hardware, coding) and full code memory (UDS $19 or KWP $18).
If the modules use the old VW protocol (TP 2.0), only the engine and transmission are found — ELM327 can\'t see the rest. This is normal.

VW\'s own parameters ($22) come from the car database: DSG oil temperature, engine oil, boost, knock, DPF soot (diesel only). On connecting the app checks which ones answer; \"(?)\" means a single source or known on another model. GM parameters are never sent to a VW.
The engine part number and software version (report.txt, \"module identification\") are the main clue for later looking up the engine, firmware and known issues.
More data: \"GM scan\" → \"Find modules\", then on the engine module a $22 scan \"F100–F1FF\" or \"1000–1FFF\". Read-only, but slow; do it parked.

string-array.name: guide_toyota
string-array.item: Toyota

The RAV4 2005 (XA20, 1AZ-FE) turned out to be on CAN 11/500 (ISO 15765-4): standard OBD works fully. The module doesn\'t report a VIN, so pick the car by hand at the top — then its protocol, socket and parameters are known.

First connection: module search (~20 s: 7E0–7E7 and addresses where Toyota often has ABS/VSC, the cluster and climate), module identification and codes. On the RAV4 2005 only the engine responds, and it rejects extended UDS requests — Toyota of this generation has its own protocol.

Toyota engine module data (service $21, as in Techstream): part of it is in the car database — ATF temperature (2182), gear and lock-up (2185), fuel in litres from the cluster — and is polled by itself. For the rest (knock, VVT-i, injection, per-cylinder misfires) there are no public formulas, so we collect raw data:

1) Start the engine, \"GM scan\" → \"Find modules\". 2) On \"Engine (7E0)\" tap \"$21\" — 256 numbers, ~20–40 s, read-only. 3) \"Tick all with data\". 4) Go to \"Main\" and drive for 15–20 minutes: warm-up, idle, accelerations, engine braking. The watched blocks are written to data.csv; from them we\'ll later work out which parameter is where.
Also there: \"Sniff bus\" (1–2 minutes with the engine running, sends nothing to the modules). If a live bus is wired to the port, you\'ll see frames with RPM, wheel speeds, etc.

If the car is on K-line (other Toyotas of that era may use ISO 9141-2 or KWP2000): connecting takes longer (BUS INIT, up to half a minute), parameters update less often, and only standard OBD is read — module search and scans are unavailable.

string-array.name: guide_lada
string-array.item: Lada
The Vesta is on CAN (ISO 15765-4): standard OBD works fully.

First connection: module search at the standard OBD addresses and a few common ABS/airbag/cluster addresses (~20 s), module identification (part number and software version) and code memory (UDS $19 or KWP $18). Read-only.

For the Vesta there is no reliable public description of AvtoVAZ\'s own parameters: live data is standard OBD. For the Granta/Kalina with the Itelma M74CAN the car database has a few (fuel rate, injection time), marked \"(?)\".
ABS, airbags and the body module sit at their own addresses, which we don\'t know, so they aren\'t searched for.
The engine module software version (report.txt, \"module identification\") is the key to the analysis: it shows which module and firmware are installed.

string-array.name: guide_hyundai
string-array.item: Hyundai
The Solaris has been made since 2011 and is usually on CAN (ISO 15765-4). If the car is a 2010 or older, it\'s most likely a different model (Accent, Verna) — check the protocol on \"Info\".

Coupe (Tiburon GK) 2003 is on K-line (KWP fast): the engine (11) and the automatic (18) answer. Besides standard OBD the app reads their numbers (KWP $1A) and full code memory (KWP $18), and on \"GM scan\" each module can be scanned with $21 and \"Tick all with data\" — so the module\'s data can be decoded later from a drive log. K-line is slow: a $21 scan takes a minute or two. Read-only.

First connection: module search at the standard OBD addresses and a few common ABS/airbag/cluster addresses (~20 s), module identification (part number and software version) and code memory (UDS $19 or KWP $18). Read-only.

Hyundai/Kia\'s own parameters come from the car database: automatic transmission fluid temperature, engine oil temperature, odometer, and the battery (BMS) on EVs. On connecting the app checks which ones answer.
ABS, airbag and body modules at their own addresses aren\'t searched for.
The engine module software version (report.txt, \"module identification\") is the key to the analysis.

string-array.name: guide_safety
string-array.item: Safety
Everything the app does on its own is read-only. Only the \"Clear\" button on \"Codes\" changes anything in the car, and it asks for confirmation.
Clearing erases not only the codes but also the readiness monitors and freeze frame — the car then has to complete its drive cycles again. Everything is saved to the session before clearing.
Scans in \"GM scan\" and bus listening: parked only. They tie up the adapter for minutes, and live data isn\'t read meanwhile.
On the road, it\'s better to let a passenger handle the app.

string-array.name: guide_files
string-array.item: What\'s in a session
raw.log — the full exchange with the adapter, timestamped: what was asked and what the car answered.
data.csv — all values over time; trip charts are built from it.
report.txt — summary: adapter, protocol, VIN, modules, their part numbers, codes, Mode 06.
scan.csv — module search and scan findings; bus.csv — bus listening.
